examples.english: Do-goodism is the faith of those who believe that human beings are innocent, regardless of the religion they practice or the country they are from; the do-gooder thinks that Europe is being mean to refugees, because the do-gooder is a fool who does not know, and does not care, that this is a form of barbaric invasion like any other; […]
examples.ref: 2017 March 26, Elvira Lindo, “Buenistas sin fronteras [Borderless do-gooders]”, in El País:
examples.text: El buenismo es la fe de los que creen que los seres humanos son inocentes, más allá de la religión que practiquen o del país del que provengan; el buenista piensa que Europa está siendo mezquina con los refugiados, porque el buenista es un insensato que no sabe, porque no se entera, que esta es una forma de invasión bárbara como otra cualquiera; […]
examples.translation: Do-goodism is the faith of those who believe that human beings are innocent, regardless of the religion they practice or the country they are from; the do-gooder thinks that Europe is being mean to refugees, because the do-gooder is a fool who does not know, and does not care, that this is a form of barbaric invasion like any other; […]

examples.english: Marta Sanza plays with all the characteristic causticness that speckles the irony found in her literary work in her prizewinning Farándula, which recently won her 18,000 euros in the 33rd Herralde Prize for novels, organised in Barcelona by the publishing house Anagrama.
examples.ref: 2015 November 2, “Marta Sanz gana el premio Herralde con ‘Farándula’”, in El País:
examples.text: Con la ironía no exenta de causticidad que caracteriza su obra literaria juega Marta Sanz con todo ello en Farándula, la obra con la que acaba de ganar en Barcelona el 33º premio Herralde de novela, dotado con 18.000 euros, que convoca la editorial Anagrama.
examples.translation: Marta Sanza plays with all the characteristic causticness that speckles the irony found in her literary work in her prizewinning Farándula, which recently won her 18,000 euros in the 33rd Herralde Prize for novels, organised in Barcelona by the publishing house Anagrama.
